context:
Work inside the existing sql_compat architecture, not around it.

1. Amend the active ADR and TODO notes first so the contract is explicit:
   DDL centralization is achieved with `schema_emit` plus `ddl_optimize`, not
   a new phase or a new resolver model.
2. Use benchbox/sql_compat/rules/ddl_optimize/starrocks_ddl_rewrites.py as
   the implementation template for every remaining adapter-owned CREATE TABLE
   rewrite. Each adapter migration should produce a rule module plus adapter
   consumer cleanup in the same slice.
3. Keep runtime-only behavior in adapters. Centralize only pure SQL rewrite
   logic; do not move catalog creation, connection/session setup, permissions,
   or other operational flow into the registry.
4. After adapter parity is achieved, remove the base
   `platform_transform_fn` hook and then clean up residual benchmark-level
   policy branches. Do not begin with a speculative schema-IR migration:
   BaseSchemaTable is not rich enough today to justify that refactor here.
5. Finish by tightening the inventory/lint/docs so new benchmark-level DDL
   monkey-patching becomes detectable and reviewable.
description:
Follow-on / amendment plan for `build-sql-compat-phase-aware-pipeline`. The ADR,
phase enum, registry, resolver, `schema_emit` rules, and the first
`ddl_optimize` rule already exist. The remaining DDL gap is narrower and more
concrete than the earlier draft assumed: many adapters still own late
`CREATE TABLE` rewrites (`_optimize_table_definition()` or Databricks
`_convert_to_delta_table()`), and base schema execution still exposes the
`platform_transform_fn` callback.

This item does NOT introduce a new `ddl_compile` phase, a new
`CompatibilityContext` shape, or a parallel `benchbox/sql_compat/transformers/`
tree. The frozen phase model is sufficient:
- `schema_emit` owns logical-to-dialect DDL policy
- `ddl_optimize` owns post-generation statement rewrites
- adapter `create_schema()` overrides keep only operational setup

Goal: finish central DDL ownership inside the shipped sql_compat architecture,
retire late adapter monkey-patching, and remove residual benchmark-level DDL
compatibility branches so benchmarks no longer need platform-specific
compatibility policy at schema generation time. If
`build-sql-compat-phase-aware-pipeline` is still active when this work starts,
fold overlapping slices into that TODO rather than landing a competing design.

anti_patterns.instead: route logical-to-dialect generation through `schema_emit` and post-generation surgery through `ddl_optimize`
anti_patterns.why: `schema_emit` and `ddl_optimize` already cover DDL ownership and are frozen in the ADR

anti_patterns.instead: add rule modules under the existing phase directories

anti_patterns.dont: extend `CompatibilityContext` with object_name, statement_kind, source_dialect, or target_dialect in this item
anti_patterns.instead: if statement metadata is required, amend the existing DDL payload contract first
anti_patterns.why: resolver specificity and plan caching are query-centric today

anti_patterns.dont: leave benchmark-local DDL compatibility branches in place once equivalent rules exist
anti_patterns.instead: delete them or reduce them to documented `@compat_local` rendering only
anti_patterns.why: shadowed inline logic defeats centralized ownership

anti_patterns.dont: move adapter operational setup into the registry
anti_patterns.instead: centralize only pure DDL statement rewrites
anti_patterns.why: catalog selection, search_path/session state, permissions, and pre-drop behavior are runtime concerns

anti_patterns.dont: promise a repo-wide schema-IR migration in this item
anti_patterns.instead: capture any proven IR gap as a separate follow-on TODO
anti_patterns.why: the current schema primitives cannot yet express all benchmark semantics cleanly

deferrals.reason: BaseSchemaTable does not currently encode vector, partition, or time-series semantics well enough to justify a repo-wide migration in this item
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] conditional-unmet: Conditional on a w16 audit proving current models can't remove local renderers; no evidence that condition was met.
deferrals.summary: Expand schema primitives / IR only if the w16 audit proves current benchmark models cannot remove remaining local renderers

deferrals.reason: Keep this item focused on SQL DDL ownership first
deferrals.summary: Unify DataFrame-mode DDL generation behind the same registry-owned path

deferrals.summary: Factor shared helper libraries across Presto/Trino/Spark-family DDL optimizers after parity is established

preserves.behavior: Adapter create_schema() methods keep operational responsibilities such as catalog/schema setup, search_path/session state, permissions, and pre-drop sequencing
Base data-loading code keeps tuning lookup, dry-run support, logging, and table-level error reporting
CompatibilityResolver.build_plan() and registry specificity remain query-centric in this item; no `CompatibilityContext` DDL-field expansion
Existing schema_emit rules for nyctaxi and tsbs_devops remain the source of truth for benchmark-level DDL compatibility policy
The Phase enum in benchbox/sql_compat/context.py remains the ADR-frozen set; do not add `ddl_compile`
The shipped StarRocks ddl_optimize rule remains authoritative and unchanged except for any shared helper extraction that preserves behavior

verifications.description: sql_compat rule and harness tests still pass after DDL-optimize expansion
Platform adapter tests covering migrated CREATE TABLE rewrites still pass
Base schema execution remains correct after hook removal
